title: A Prior-Aware Metric for Efficiently Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2602.18733v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Training data leakage from Large Language Models (LLMs) raises serious concerns related to privacy, security, and copyright compliance. A central challenge in assessing this risk is distinguishing prefix-specific memorization of training data from the generation of statistically common sequences. Existing approaches to measuring memorization often conflate these phenomena, labeling outputs as memorized even when they arise from generalization over common patterns. Counterfactual memorization and other related metrics \citep{zhang2023counterfactual, wang2025generalization, lesci2024causal} provide principled solutions, however, their reliance on retraining multiple baseline models or parsing through the training data makes them computationally impractical at scale.   This work introduces \emph{Prior-Aware memorization}, a theoretically grounded, lightweight and training-free criterion for identifying prefix-specific memorization in LL

translated_title: 一种用于高效区分大型语言模型中记忆与泛化的先验感知度量
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）的训练数据泄露引发了与隐私、安全和版权合规相关的严重担忧。评估这一风险的核心挑战在于区分训练数据的前缀特定记忆与统计常见序列的生成。现有的记忆测量方法常常混淆这些现象，即使输出源于对常见模式的泛化，也会将其标记为记忆。反事实记忆及其他相关指标提供了原则性解决方案，然而，它们依赖重新训练多个基线模型或解析训练数据，使得在大规模场景下计算上不可行。本工作引入了“先验感知记忆”（Prior-Aware memorization），这是一种有理论依据、轻量级且无需训练的准则，用于识别LLM中的前缀特定记忆。
tldr: 本文提出了一种轻量级、无需训练的先验感知记忆度量方法，能有效区分大型语言模型中的前缀特定记忆与泛化现象，避免了现有方法的高计算成本。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a lightweight, training-free prior-aware memorization metric that effectively distinguishes prefix-specific memorization from generalization in large language models, avoiding the high computational costs of existing methods.
